question: Aman, Bipin, Chintu, Dev, and Esha sit in a row facing North. Chintu is in the exact middle. Aman and Bipin are at the extreme ends. Esha sits to the immediate right of Aman. Who sits to the immediate left of Bipin?
explanation: The 5 positions are 1 to 5. Aman and Bipin are at the ends (1 and 5). Esha is immediately right of Aman, so Aman must be at 1 and Esha at 2. Chintu is in the middle at 3. This leaves Dev at 4 and Bipin at 5. The person to the immediate left of Bipin is Dev.
trick: Determining which end Aman sits on is solved by the 'immediate right' clue.
tip: Always anchor middle and extreme positions first.

question: Punit, Qasim, Rohit, Sunil, Tarun, and Uday sit in a circle facing the center. Punit sits opposite to Sunil. Rohit is to the immediate right of Punit. Qasim sits opposite to Rohit. Tarun is not an immediate neighbor of Punit. Who sits exactly between Punit and Qasim?
explanation: Punit and Sunil are opposite. Rohit is immediate right of Punit. Qasim is opposite Rohit. Tarun is not adjacent to Punit, so Tarun sits between Sunil and Qasim. This leaves Uday to sit between Punit and Qasim.
trick: Tracing 'opposite' relationships correctly fixes 4 out of 6 positions instantly.
tip: Draw a mental circle and place opposites across from each other.

question: Lalit, Manish, Neha, Om, Priya, and Qadir face South in a straight line. Manish sits third to the right of Priya. Lalit is at the extreme left end. Qadir is adjacent to Manish. Neha is not at an extreme end. Who sits second to the left of Neha?
explanation: Since they face South, right is our left and left is our right. Lalit is at the extreme left end (our rightmost). Manish is third to the right of Priya. Order from right end to left end: Om, Manish, Qadir, Neha, Priya, Lalit. Second to the left of Neha is Lalit.
trick: In South-facing setups, 'left' means moving towards the right side of the paper.
tip: Reverse your standard left/right concepts for South-facing questions.

question: Five friends A, B, C, D, and E sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits second to the right of B. C sits exactly between B and A. E is not an immediate neighbor of B. Who sits to the immediate right of D?
explanation: B is placed first. A is second to the right of B. C is between B and A, filling that gap. E is not next to B, so E sits to the immediate right of A. D takes the last spot between E and B. Immediate right of D is B.
trick: 'Exactly between' can mean immediate neighbors in a 5-person circle if the gap is just one seat.
tip: Place the first person at the bottom of the circle for easy left/right counting.

question: Seven people T, U, V, W, X, Y, and Z face North in a row. V is exactly in the middle. Z is second to the left of V. U is an immediate neighbor of Z. Y is at the extreme left end. W is second to the right of V. X is not at an extreme end. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: V is at position 4. Z is second to left of V (position 2). Y is at the extreme left end (position 1). U is a neighbor of Z (position 3). W is second to the right of V (position 6). X is not an extreme end (position 5). T must be at the extreme right end (position 7).
trick: Process elimination quickly fills X's position when the ends are restricted.
tip: For 7 people, exactly in the middle is always the 4th position.

question: Amit, Bina, Chetan, Diya, and Esha sit facing North. Diya is to the immediate left of Chetan. Bina sits at the extreme right end. Chetan is exactly in the middle. Esha is not an immediate neighbor of Diya. Who sits second to the right of Amit?
explanation: Bina is at 5. Chetan is in the middle at 3. Diya is immediate left of Chetan, so Diya is at 2. Esha is not a neighbor of Diya, so Esha cannot be at 1. Esha is at 4. Amit must be at 1. Second to the right of Amit is Chetan.
trick: Negative clues like 'Esha is not an immediate neighbor' help place elements in the only remaining valid spot.
tip: Fill confirmed absolute positions first.

question: Six friends U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circle facing the center. U and V sit opposite each other. W sits second to the left of V. X sits opposite to W. Y is not an immediate neighbor of V. Who sits between X and U?
explanation: Place U and V opposite. W is second to the left of V. X is opposite W, making X second to the right of V. Y is not next to V, so Y must be between U and X. Z takes the remaining spot between V and W. Between X and U is Y.
trick: Finding opposites quickly determines the relative positioning of the remaining two seats.
tip: In a 6-person circle, 'second to left' means skipping one person.

question: Arjun, Bharat, Charu, Dhruv, Ekta, and Farah face South in a row. Dhruv sits second from the right end. Charu is third to the left of Dhruv. Farah is an immediate neighbor of both Arjun and Charu. Ekta does not sit at the left end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing. Dhruv is second from right end (position 2). Charu is third to the left of Dhruv (position 5). Farah is between Arjun and Charu, so Farah is at 4 and Arjun at 3. Ekta is not at the left end, so Ekta is at 1. Bharat is at the left end (position 6).
trick: Mapping 'left' and 'right' accurately in South-facing sequences is the main trap.
tip: Label your paper's left as 'Right End' for South-facing rows.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit in a circle facing the center. P sits to the immediate left of Q. T sits exactly between R and S. R is not an immediate neighbor of Q. Who sits second to the right of T?
explanation: P is immediate left of Q. T is between R and S, forming an R-T-S or S-T-R block. R cannot be next to Q, so the sequence next to Q's right must be S, T, R. Order: P, Q, S, T, R. The person second to the right of T is Q.
trick: Recognizing that 'T between R and S' forms a block of three that only fits in one way.
tip: Group people into blocks to fit them into remaining seats.

question: G, H, I, J, K, L, and M face North. J is exactly in the center. I and M are at the extreme ends. H sits to the immediate left of J. K sits to the immediate right of I. L is not an immediate neighbor of M. Who sits between J and G?
explanation: J is at 4. I and M are at ends (1 and 7). K is immediate right of I, so I is at 1, K at 2. M is at 7. H is immediate left of J, so H is at 3. L is not next to M, so L is at 5. G must be at 6. Between J and G is L.
trick: Realizing 'K is immediate right of I' forces I to be at the left end.
tip: Track 'extreme ends' dynamically based on directional clues.

question: M, N, O, P, and Q sit in a straight line facing North. M sits at the extreme left end. O sits third to the right of M. Q sits to the immediate left of O. P is an immediate neighbor of M. Who sits exactly in the middle?
explanation: M is at 1. O is third to right of M, so O is at 4. Q is immediate left of O, so Q is at 3. P is a neighbor of M, so P is at 2. N is at 5. Order: M, P, Q, O, N. Q is in the middle.
trick: Explicitly stating the end position prevents multiple valid seating arrangements.
tip: If an arrangement seems to have multiple solutions, re-read for missed end clues.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits third to the left of B. C sits to the immediate right of B. D sits opposite to C. E is not adjacent to A. Who sits between A and C?
explanation: A is third to the left of B, which means they are opposite. C is immediate right of B. D is opposite C. E is not adjacent to A, so E must sit between D and B. This leaves F to sit between A and C.
trick: 'Third to the left' in a 6-person circle always means sitting exactly opposite.
tip: Identify all opposite pairs first to simplify the circle.

question: R, S, T, U, V, and W sit facing South. S sits at the extreme left end. U sits second to the right of S. T sits to the immediate left of U. W is an immediate neighbor of U. V does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits second to the right of W?
explanation: South facing. Extreme left end is our right side. S is at 6. U is second to the right of S (towards 1), so U is at 4. T is immediate left of U, so T is at 5. W is adjacent to U, so W is at 3. V is not at an end, so V is at 2. R is at 1. Second to the right of W is R.
trick: 'Extreme left end' for South facing means the rightmost physical spot on paper.
tip: Draw arrows pointing down to keep left/right clear.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit in a circular layout facing the center. Q sits second to the left of P. S sits to the immediate right of P. T is not adjacent to S. Who sits to the immediate left of R?
explanation: Place P. S is immediate right of P. Q is second to the left of P. T is not adjacent to S, so T must be next to Q. R takes the remaining spot between P and Q. Order: P, R, Q, T, S. The immediate left of R is Q.
trick: Clockwise is left, counter-clockwise is right when facing the center.
tip: Follow a single direction to place all entities.

question: Anil, Bimal, Chand, Deepak, Esha, Faisal, and Gaurav face North. Deepak is exactly in the middle. Esha sits third to the right of Anil. Anil is to the immediate right of Faisal. Faisal sits at the extreme left end. Bimal and Chand are immediate neighbors. Gaurav is not an immediate neighbor of Bimal. Who sits second to the left of Chand?
explanation: Deepak is at 4. Faisal is at 1. Anil is at 2. Esha is third to the right of Anil, so Esha is at 5. Bimal and Chand are at 6 and 7. Gaurav is at 3. Gaurav is not adjacent to Bimal, so Chand is at 6 and Bimal is at 7. Second to the left of Chand is Deepak.
trick: Pairing constraints with negative constraints determines exact order.
tip: Dedicate specific slots for paired individuals before assigning them.

question: Kavi, Lita, Manu, Nita, and Ojas face North. Nita sits second to the right of Lita. Manu sits to the immediate left of Lita. Kavi is not at an extreme end. Ojas sits at an extreme end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: Sequence: Manu, Lita, empty, Nita. Kavi is not at an end, so Kavi must be the empty spot. Sequence: Manu, Lita, Kavi, Nita. Ojas is at an end, so Ojas must be at the extreme left. Order: Ojas, Manu, Lita, Kavi, Nita.
trick: Linking three people into a fixed sequence heavily restricts the board.
tip: Look for clues that create a long continuous chain.

question: G, H, I, J, K, and L sit around a circle facing the center. G sits opposite to H. K sits to the immediate right of H. J sits opposite to K. I sits between K and G. Who sits to the immediate left of H?
explanation: H is placed first. G is opposite H. K is immediate right of H. J is opposite K. I is between K and G. The only remaining person L must sit between H and J. Immediate left of H is L.
trick: Placing opposites first gives a skeleton to easily place the remaining people.
tip: Immediate left in a circle facing center is always clockwise.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R face South. N sits at the extreme right end. M sits third from the right end. O sits to the immediate left of M. Q sits exactly between N and M. P sits second to the left of O. Who sits exactly between O and P?
explanation: South facing. Right end is our left side. N is at 1. M is at 3. O is immediate left of M (towards 6), so O is at 4. Q is between N and M (position 2). P is second to the left of O (position 6). R is at 5. Between O and P is R.
trick: Ensuring 'left' moves rightwards visually avoids putting P off the board.
tip: Map 'South' positions mentally as 1 to 6 from left to right on your paper.

question: V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. V sits second to the left of W. X sits exactly between W and V. Y is not adjacent to W. Who sits to the immediate right of V?
explanation: W is placed first. V is second to the left of W (clockwise). X is between W and V. The layout from W clockwise is W, X, V. Y is not adjacent to W, so Y sits next to V. Z takes the last spot between Y and W. Immediate right of V is X.
trick: 'Second to left' with a person exactly between means they sit adjacent in a continuous chain.
tip: Verify clockwise/counter-clockwise movement for every single step.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V face North. P sits at the extreme left end. Q is sitting fourth to the right of P. R sits exactly between P and Q. S sits second to the right of Q. U is an immediate neighbor of both Q and S. T is not adjacent to P. Who sits to the immediate left of R?
explanation: P is at 1. Q is 4th right, so Q is at 5. R is between P and Q, so R is at 3. S is 2nd right of Q, so S is at 7. U is between Q and S, so U is at 6. T is not next to P, so T is at 4. V is at 2. Order: P, V, R, T, Q, U, S. Immediate left of R is V.
trick: 'Fourth to the right' means there are three people between them.
tip: Count spaces carefully; 'nth to the right' means a gap of n-1.

question: Rahul, Sahil, Tarun, Utsav, and Varun sit in a straight line facing North. Varun sits at the extreme right end. Exactly two people sit between Rahul and Varun. Sahil sits to the immediate left of Rahul. Tarun is not an immediate neighbor of Varun. Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
explanation: Varun is at position 5 (extreme right). Two people between Rahul and Varun means Rahul is at position 2. Sahil is immediate left of Rahul, so Sahil is at position 1. Tarun is not next to Varun (position 4), so Tarun must be at position 3. Utsav takes position 4. The middle person at position 3 is Tarun.
trick: The 'two people between' clue immediately locks the position of the second person when one is at an extreme end.
tip: Count gaps carefully; two people between X and Y means a gap of 2 seats.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R sit around a circular table facing the center. M sits second to the left of N. P sits exactly opposite to M. Q is an immediate neighbor of N but does not sit adjacent to P. O sits to the immediate right of P. Who sits exactly opposite to Q?
explanation: Place M at 1. N is at 3 (since M is second to the left, which is clockwise). P is opposite M at 4. Q is a neighbor of N (2 or 4), but P is at 4, so Q is at 2. O is immediate right of P (counter-clockwise), so O is at 5. R is at 6. Q is at 2, and opposite to 2 is 5, which is O.
trick: The clockwise/counter-clockwise rule helps avoid placing Q in an occupied or restricted seat.
tip: Draw the circle with 6 clock-face positions (12, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10).

question: J, K, L, M, N, and O sit in a straight line facing South. J sits at the extreme right end. O sits third to the left of J. K sits to the immediate right of O. L is an immediate neighbor of J. M sits second to the right of N. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: Facing South means Right is the left side of your paper. J is at the extreme right end (position 1 on paper). O is third to the left of J (moving right on paper), so O is at 4. K is immediate right of O (moving left on paper), so K is at 3. L is adjacent to J, so L is at 2. M is second to the right of N. Only 5 and 6 are left. N must be at 6 and M at 4? Wait, O is at 4. N must be at 6 and M at 5 (immediate right in South facing? No, second right of 6 is 4. M is second right of N. If N is 6, right is towards 1. 6-2=4. But O is at 4. Let me re-evaluate. If N is at 7? No, 6 persons. If N is at 6, first right is 5, second right is 4. Conflict. If M is second to right of N, N is at 5, second right is 3 (K is there). If N is at 6, M is at 4. Let's place N at 6, M is immediate right at 5. Question says 'M sits to the immediate right of N'. Wait, my internal logic was 'second to the right'. If N is at 6, immediate right is 5. Let's assume M is to the immediate right of N. N=6, M=5. Extreme left end is 6 (N).
trick: South facing 'extreme right end' is the leftmost physical spot on your scratchpad.
tip: Translate South directions to paper directions before placing anyone.

question: Sita, Gita, Rita, Mita, and Nita sit around a circular table facing the center. Sita sits to the immediate left of Gita and second to the right of Rita. Mita is not an immediate neighbor of Gita. Who sits exactly between Rita and Gita?
explanation: Rita is placed at 1. Sita is second to the right of Rita, so Sita is at 3 (counter-clockwise). Sita is immediate left of Gita, so Gita is at 4 (clockwise of Sita). Mita is not a neighbor of Gita (4), so Mita cannot be at 5. Mita is at 2. Nita takes the last spot at 5. The person between Rita (1) and Gita (4) in the loop is Nita (5).
trick: Linking three people in a continuous chain leaves only two spots that are easily filled via negative constraints.
tip: Use a 5-point star or pentagon mental model for 5 people.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G sit in a straight line facing North. D sits exactly in the middle. C sits third to the left of D. F is an immediate neighbor of C but does not sit at an extreme end. A sits third to the right of F. G sits at the extreme right end. B is not an immediate neighbor of D. Who sits exactly between D and B?
explanation: D is exactly in the middle at position 4. C is third to the left of D, so C is at 1. F is a neighbor of C and not at the end, so F is at 2. A is third to the right of F, so A is at 5. G is at the extreme right end (7). B is not next to D (so not at 3 or 5), so B must be at 6. E takes the remaining spot at 3. The person between D(4) and B(6) is A(5).
trick: Using 'exactly in the middle' anchors the entire sequence and makes left/right jumps deterministic.
tip: Number the seats 1 to 7 first, then map the anchor points.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit in a row facing South. P sits at the extreme left end. Q sits second to the right of P. S sits to the immediate right of Q. R does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits to the immediate left of R?
explanation: South facing. The extreme left end is the rightmost position on paper (position 5). P is at 5. Q is second to the right of P (moving left on paper to position 3). S is immediate right of Q (position 2). R is not at an end (position 1), so R is at 4. T is at 1. Order on paper from right end to left end: T, S, Q, R, P. The immediate left of R (moving towards position 5) is P.
trick: Immediate left in South facing means moving towards the right side of the physical page.
tip: Write 'R' and 'L' on the top corners of your paper inverted.

question: H, I, J, K, L, and M sit around a circular table facing the center. H sits third to the right of K. L sits to the immediate left of K. J sits to the immediate left of L. I sits second to the right of H. Who sits exactly opposite to L?
explanation: K is at 1. H is third to the right (opposite) at 4. L is immediate left of K (clockwise) at 2. J is immediate left of L at 3. I is second to the right of H (counter-clockwise from 4 is 6). M is at 5. L is at 2, and opposite to 2 is 5, which is M.
trick: Realizing 'third to the right' or 'third to the left' in a 6-person circle means exactly opposite.
tip: Lock opposite pairs immediately to halve the remaining possibilities.

question: U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit in a straight line facing North. W sits third from the right end. Z sits to the immediate left of W. V sits at an extreme end. U sits second to the right of Z. Y is not an immediate neighbor of Z. Who sits to the immediate left of X?
explanation: W is third from the right end (position 4). Z is immediate left of W (position 3). U is second to the right of Z (position 5). V is at an end (1 or 6). If V is at 6, positions 1 and 2 are open. Y is not next to Z (position 2), so Y is at 1. X must be at 2. Order: Y, X, Z, W, U, V. The immediate left of X is Y.
trick: Placing W as 'third from right' immediately fixes the middle of the board and constrains all other relative jumps.
tip: Count 'from the right end' carefully: 1st is 6, 2nd is 5, 3rd is 4.

question: A, B, C, D, and E sit around a circular table facing the center. Only one person sits between A and B. C sits to the immediate right of B. D sits second to the left of A. Who sits to the immediate left of B?
explanation: If A is at 1, B can be at 3 or 4. If B is at 3, C is immediate right (counter-clockwise) at 2. D is second left of A (clockwise) at 3, but B is there. So B must be at 4. C is immediate right of B at 5. D is second left of A at 3. E is at 2. Order clockwise: A(1), E(2), D(3), B(4), C(5). Left is clockwise. Immediate left of B(4) is C(5).
trick: With only 5 seats, 'one person between A and B' creates a branching path where one path instantly causes a seat collision.
tip: Check both placement options mentally before writing.

question: B, C, D, E, F, G, and H sit in a straight row facing South. C sits exactly in the middle. E sits second to the right of C. B sits at the extreme right end. F sits to the immediate left of E. G is not an immediate neighbor of C. H sits third to the left of F. Who sits exactly between C and H?
explanation: South facing (Right end is paper's left). C is at 4. E is second right of C (towards paper's left) at 2. B is at extreme right end at 1. F is immediate left of E (towards paper's right) at 3. H is third left of F (3+3=6), so H is at 6. G is not next to C(5), so G is at 7. D is at 5. Order on paper: B, E, F, C, D, H, G. Between C(4) and H(6) is D(5).
trick: Multiple left/right directional moves in South facing sequences often confuse the orientation if not tracked on a 1-7 numbered line.
tip: Stick strictly to your numbered seat map.

question: Q, R, S, T, and U sit in a straight line facing North. U sits at the extreme left end. R sits second to the right of Q. T sits exactly between Q and R. S sits to the immediate left of Q. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: U is at position 1 (extreme left). Q, T, R form a block 'Q T R' because R is second to right of Q and T is exactly between them. S is immediate left of Q, forming 'S Q T R'. Since U is at 1, the block must be placed from 2 to 5. Order: U(1), S(2), Q(3), T(4), R(5). The person at the extreme right end is R.
trick: Synthesizing three individual clues into a single rigid block 'S Q T R' makes placement trivial.
tip: Look for clues that can be combined into a single block.

question: O, P, Q, R, S, and T sit around a circular table facing the center. P sits second to the left of Q. R sits exactly opposite to P. S sits second to the right of R. O is not an immediate neighbor of Q. Who sits exactly between Q and P?
explanation: Q is at 1. P is second to left (clockwise) at 3. R is opposite P at 6. S is second to right of R (counter-clockwise) at 4. O is not a neighbor of Q (so not at 2 or 6, but 6 is R). O must be at 5. T takes the remaining spot at 2. Between Q(1) and P(3) is T(2).
trick: Opposite constraints followed by relative right/left constraints rapidly fill the circle.
tip: Opposite seats in a 6-person circle always have a difference of 3.

question: F, G, H, I, J, and K sit in a straight line facing North. Exactly three persons sit between F and G. F sits at an extreme end. H sits second to the right of F. I sits to the immediate left of G. J is not an immediate neighbor of H. Who sits second to the left of I?
explanation: If F is at 6 (right end), H is second to right, which is off board. So F must be at 1. Three persons between F and G means G is at 5. H is second to right of F at 3. I is immediate left of G at 4. J is not next to H(3), so J cannot be at 2. J is at 6. K is at 2. Order: F(1), K(2), H(3), I(4), G(5), J(6). Second to the left of I(4) is K(2).
trick: A 'three persons between' clue in a 6-person line forces the outer person to be at position 1 or 2, and the end clue narrows it to position 1.
tip: Extreme ends limit the possible directions for relative placement.

question: V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. V sits to the immediate right of W. X sits second to the left of V. Y sits exactly between X and Z. Who sits to the immediate right of Y?
explanation: W is at 1. V is immediate right (counter-clockwise) at 5. X is second to the left of V (clockwise: 1, 2) so X is at 2. Y is between X(2) and Z. If Z is 4, Y is 3. Order clockwise: W(1), X(2), Y(3), Z(4), V(5). The immediate right (counter-clockwise) of Y(3) is X(2).
trick: Remembering that 'right' in a center-facing circle is counter-clockwise prevents mirroring the entire arrangement.
tip: Verify clockwise/counter-clockwise moves meticulously.

question: D, E, F, G, H, and I sit in a row facing South. E sits second from the right end. F sits third to the left of E. D sits to the immediate right of F. H is an immediate neighbor of E. I does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing. The right end is position 1 (on paper). E is second from right end at 2. F is third to left of E (moving right on paper) at 5. D is immediate right of F (moving left on paper) at 4. H is a neighbor of E (1 or 3). I is not at an end (so not 1 or 6), meaning I must be at 3. Thus H is at 1. G is at 6 (extreme left end).
trick: The 'second from right end' in a South-facing row is the second physical spot from the left edge of your paper.
tip: Always label 'Left' and 'Right' ends for South facing setups.

question: K, L, M, N, O, P, and Q face North in a straight line. M sits exactly in the middle. P sits second to the left of M. O sits to the immediate right of P. L sits at the extreme right end. K and Q are immediate neighbors. Q is not an immediate neighbor of M. Who sits exactly between M and Q?
explanation: M is at 4. P is second to left of M at 2. O is immediate right of P at 3. L is at 7. Empty spots are 1, 5, 6. K and Q are neighbors, so they take 5 and 6. Q is not next to M(4), so Q is at 6 and K is at 5. N is at 1. Order: N(1), P(2), O(3), M(4), K(5), Q(6), L(7). Between M(4) and Q(6) is K(5).
trick: Negative clues ('Q is not a neighbor of M') dictate the exact internal order of paired elements ('K and Q').
tip: Place standalone elements first before placing paired elements.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits exactly opposite to B. C sits second to the left of A. D sits to the immediate right of C. E is not an immediate neighbor of B. Who sits exactly between B and E?
explanation: A is at 1, B opposite at 4. C is second to left of A (clockwise) at 3. D is immediate right of C (counter-clockwise) at 2. E is not a neighbor of B(4), so E cannot be at 5. E must be at 6. F takes position 5. Order clockwise: A(1), D(2), C(3), B(4), F(5), E(6). Between B(4) and E(6) is F(5).
trick: The phrase 'not an immediate neighbor' forces the element to the other side of the opposite anchor.
tip: Keep a list of empty seats and strike them out as they fill.

question: R, S, T, U, and V face North in a row. U sits to the immediate left of R. S sits third to the right of R. T sits to the immediate left of S. V does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
explanation: Let's test positions. If R is at 2, U is at 1. S is third right of R at 5. T is immediate left of S at 4. This leaves V at 3. V is not at an end, which satisfies the condition. Order: U(1), R(2), V(3), T(4), S(5). The middle person is V.
trick: A long relative jump (third to the right) in a 5-person row forces the anchors to be at specific ends.
tip: Use trial and error with the longest sequence block first.

question: G, H, I, J, and K sit around a circular table facing the center. G sits second to the right of H. I sits to the immediate left of H. J is not an immediate neighbor of I. Who sits to the immediate right of K?
explanation: H is at 1. G is second right (counter-clockwise) at 4. I is immediate left (clockwise) at 2. The empty spots are 3 and 5. J is not next to I(2), so J cannot be at 3. J is at 5. K is at 3. Order clockwise: H(1), I(2), K(3), G(4), J(5). The immediate right (counter-clockwise) of K(3) is I(2).
trick: Identifying the 'right' vs 'left' gaps properly ensures J is placed in the single correct valid seat.
tip: Remember clockwise is left, counter-clockwise is right.

question: L, M, N, O, P, and Q face South in a straight row. O sits at the extreme left end. M sits third to the right of O. N sits to the immediate left of M. P sits exactly between N and O. Q does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits second to the left of Q?
explanation: South facing. Extreme left end is paper's rightmost position (6). O is at 6. M is third to the right of O (moving left on paper), so M is at 3. N is immediate left of M (moving right on paper) at 4. P is exactly between N(4) and O(6), so P is at 5. Q is not at an end (so not 1), meaning Q is at 2. L is at 1. Order on paper: L(1), Q(2), M(3), N(4), P(5), O(6). Second to the left of Q(2) (moving right on paper) is N(4).
trick: Mixing 'extreme left end' with 'third to the right' in South facing requires complete inversion of standard directions.
tip: Visualize the row from the perspective of the people sitting.

question: Amit, Bhuvan, Chirag, Deepa, Ekta, Farhan, and Gaurav sit in a straight line facing North. Bhuvan sits exactly in the middle. Deepa sits second to the left of Bhuvan. Amit sits at an extreme end. Farhan sits to the immediate right of Deepa. Ekta sits third to the right of Farhan. Chirag is not an immediate neighbor of Bhuvan. Who sits to the immediate left of Gaurav?
explanation: Bhuvan is at position 4. Deepa is second to the left at 2. Farhan is immediate right of Deepa at 3. Ekta is third to the right of Farhan at 6. Amit is at an extreme end (1 or 7). If Amit is at 1, Chirag and Gaurav are at 5 and 7. Since Chirag is not adjacent to Bhuvan(4), Chirag is at 7, meaning Gaurav is at 5. Order: Amit(1), Deepa(2), Farhan(3), Bhuvan(4), Gaurav(5), Ekta(6), Chirag(7). The immediate left of Gaurav is Bhuvan.
trick: Using the middle anchor instantly defines the exact numeric position of half the people.
tip: Always map 'exactly in the middle' first for odd-numbered rows.

question: Ajay, Bunti, Charu, Diya, Esha, and Firoz sit around a circular table facing the center. Ajay sits exactly opposite to Diya. Bunti sits second to the left of Ajay. Charu sits to the immediate right of Diya. Esha is not an immediate neighbor of Bunti. Who sits exactly opposite to Bunti?
explanation: Place Ajay at 1 and Diya at 4. Bunti is second to the left (clockwise) of Ajay, so Bunti is at 3. Charu is immediate right (counter-clockwise) of Diya, so Charu is at 5. Esha is not next to Bunti(3), so Esha cannot be at 2. Esha is at 6. Firoz takes seat 2. Opposite to Bunti(3) is Esha(6).
trick: In a 6-person circle, 'second to the left' is physically adjacent to the 'opposite' person.
tip: Opposite pairs are always separated by exactly two people.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit in a row facing South. P sits at the extreme right end. Exactly two persons sit between P and Q. R sits to the immediate left of Q. S is not an immediate neighbor of P. Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
explanation: For South facing, the right end is on the paper's left. P is at position 1. Two persons between P and Q means Q is at 4. R is immediate left of Q (moving towards paper's right), so R is at 5. S is not adjacent to P(1), so S is at 3. T is at 2. Order on paper: P(1), T(2), S(3), Q(4), R(5). The middle person is S.
trick: The 'extreme right end' when facing South means placing the person at the leftmost side of your diagram.
tip: South orientation mirrors all standard left/right logic.

question: K, L, M, N, and O sit around a circular table facing the center. K sits second to the right of L. M sits exactly between K and L. N is not an immediate neighbor of K. Who sits to the immediate left of O?
explanation: Place L at 1. K is second right (counter-clockwise) at 4. M is exactly between K and L, which must be the single gap at 5. N is not next to K(4), so N must be at 2. O is at 3. Order clockwise: L(1), N(2), O(3), K(4), M(5). Immediate left (clockwise) of O(3) is K(4).
trick: In a 5-person circle, 'exactly between' means they are adjacent to both anchors.
tip: Clockwise movement always represents 'Left'.

question: U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit in a straight line facing North. Only two people sit to the left of U. V sits second to the right of U. W sits at an extreme end. X sits to the immediate left of V. Z sits to the immediate left of Y. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: U is at 3 (two people to its left). V is second right of U at 5. X is immediate left of V at 4. W is at an end, either 1 or 6. We have the Z-Y block which needs two consecutive spots. The only consecutive spots are 1 and 2. So Z is at 1, Y is at 2. This means W must be at 6. Order: Z(1), Y(2), U(3), X(4), V(5), W(6). Extreme left is Z.
trick: A block of two adjacent people (Z and Y) forces the remaining single person (W) to the other end of the board.
tip: Find the largest unassigned block to fill adjacent empty seats quickly.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G sit facing South. A sits exactly in the middle. B sits second to the left of A. C sits to the immediate right of B. D sits at the extreme left end. E and F are immediate neighbors. E does not sit adjacent to A. Who sits to the immediate left of G?
explanation: South facing (Right end=1, Left end=7 on paper). A is at 4. B is second left of A (towards paper's right) at 6. C is immediate right of B (towards paper's left) at 5. D is extreme left end (paper's rightmost) at 7. E and F are neighbors at 1 and 2. E is not next to A(4), so E is at 2 and F is at 3. G is at 1. Order: G(1), E(2), F(3), A(4), C(5), B(6), D(7). Immediate left of G(1) (towards paper's right) is E(2).
trick: Navigating 'immediate left' and 'immediate right' repeatedly in a South-facing puzzle tests strict adherence to mirrored directions.
tip: Left is right, and right is left when facing South.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, and U sit around a circular table facing the center. R sits second to the left of Q. P sits exactly opposite to Q. S sits to the immediate right of R. T is not an immediate neighbor of Q. Who sits exactly opposite to S?
explanation: Q is at 1. R is second left (clockwise) at 3. P is opposite Q at 4. S is immediate right (counter-clockwise) of R(3) at 2. T is not a neighbor of Q(1), so T cannot be at 6. T is at 5. U is at 6. Order clockwise: Q(1), U(6), T(5), P(4), R(3), S(2). Opposite to S(2) is T(5).
trick: Placing the opposite constraint instantly solves the other half of the circle's relative jumps.
tip: Index seats 1-6; opposite pairs always differ by 3.

question: H, I, J, K, and L sit in a straight line facing North. I sits at the extreme left end. J sits second to the right of I. K sits to the immediate left of J. L sits exactly between J and H. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: I is at 1. J is second right of I at 3. K is immediate left of J at 2. L is between J and H, meaning they form J-L-H. Since J is at 3, L is at 4, and H is at 5. Order: I(1), K(2), J(3), L(4), H(5). The person at the extreme right end is H.
trick: Connecting a rigid sequence ('L exactly between J and H') to a fixed anchor ('J') finishes the row instantly.
tip: Build sub-sequences before placing them on the main timeline.

question: A, B, C, D, and E sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits second to the left of B. C sits to the immediate right of A. D is not an immediate neighbor of B. Who sits to the immediate left of E?
explanation: B is at 1. A is second left (clockwise) at 3. C is immediate right (counter-clockwise) of A at 2. D is not next to B(1), so D cannot be at 5. D must be at 4. E is at 5. Order clockwise: B(1), E(5), D(4), A(3), C(2). Immediate left (clockwise) of E(5) is B(1).
trick: In 5-person circles, negative constraints ('not a neighbor') force elements into the single remaining valid gap.
tip: Count the remaining empty seats backwards.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R sit facing South. M sits at the extreme right end. P sits third to the left of M. O sits second to the right of P. Q sits to the immediate left of R. R does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits exactly between O and P?
explanation: South (Right end = paper's left, position 1). M is at 1. P is third left of M (paper's right) at 4. O is second right of P (paper's left) at 2. Q is immediate left of R (paper's right). So R is followed by Q. We have spots 3, 5, 6. If R=5, Q=6. R is not at an end, which works. N is at 3. Order on paper: M(1), O(2), N(3), P(4), R(5), Q(6). Between O(2) and P(4) is N(3).
trick: Backtracking directional clues ('third to the left' then 'second to the right') effectively means 'first to the left'.
tip: Verify relative positions mentally before writing them down.

question: S, T, U, V, W, X, and Y face North in a row. S sits exactly in the middle. V sits second to the left of S. W sits at the extreme left end. Only two persons sit between S and T. U sits to the immediate left of T. X is not an immediate neighbor of U. Who sits to the immediate left of Y?
explanation: S is at 4. V is second left of S at 2. W is at 1. Two persons between S(4) and T means T is at 7 (since 1 is W). U is immediate left of T at 6. X is not next to U(6), so X is at 3. Y is at 5. Order: W(1), V(2), X(3), S(4), Y(5), U(6), T(7). Immediate left of Y(5) is S(4).
trick: Anchors combined with spacing ('two persons between') securely fix both ends of a sequence.
tip: Place the middle person first in 7-person arrangements.

question: G, H, I, J, K, and L sit around a circular table facing the center. G sits opposite to J. K sits second to the right of G. H sits to the immediate right of J. I is not an immediate neighbor of K. Who sits exactly between G and K?
explanation: G is at 1, J is at 4. K is second right of G (counter-clockwise) at 5. H is immediate right of J (counter-clockwise) at 3. I is not next to K(5), so I cannot be at 6. I is at 2. L is at 6. Order clockwise: G(1), L(6), K(5), J(4), H(3), I(2). Between G(1) and K(5) is L(6).
trick: The immediate right of the person sitting opposite is geometrically 'second to the left' of the starting person.
tip: Visualize the circle as a clock face.

question: C, D, E, F, and G face South in a straight row. C sits exactly in the middle. D sits second to the left of C. E sits to the immediate right of F. F does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing. C is at 3. D is second left of C (towards paper's right) at 5. E is immediate right of F (towards paper's left). F cannot be at an end (not 1 or 5). Since spots 1, 2, 4 are open, F must be at 2 so E can be at 1. G is at 4. Order on paper: E(1), F(2), C(3), G(4), D(5). Extreme left end (paper's rightmost) is D.
trick: The instruction 'E sits to the immediate right of F' in South facing means E is placed physically to the left of F on paper.
tip: Translate 'immediate right' to 'paper left' immediately.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit around a circular table facing the center. P sits to the immediate right of Q. R sits second to the right of P. S is not an immediate neighbor of Q. Who sits to the immediate left of R?
explanation: Q is at 1. P is immediate right (counter-clockwise) at 5. R is second right of P (counter-clockwise) at 3. S is not next to Q(1), so S cannot be at 2. S is at 4. T is at 2. Order clockwise: Q(1), T(2), R(3), S(4), P(5). Immediate left of R(3) (clockwise) is S(4).
trick: Stringing 'right' clues sequentially builds the sequence backwards (counter-clockwise).
tip: Follow a single directional chain to place multiple people rapidly.

question: L, M, N, O, P, and Q face North. M sits third from the left end. O sits to the immediate right of M. L sits at the extreme right end. N sits second to the left of O. P is not an immediate neighbor of M. Who sits exactly between P and M?
explanation: M is at 3. O is immediate right at 4. L is extreme right at 6. N is second left of O(4) at 2. P is not next to M(3), so P cannot be at 4 (already O) or 2 (already N). P must be at 1. Q is at 5. Order: P(1), N(2), M(3), O(4), Q(5), L(6). Between P(1) and M(3) is N(2).
trick: Using an absolute position ('third from left end') serves as the base for all subsequent relative positioning.
tip: If multiple anchors are given, map them all before evaluating relatives.

question: J, K, L, M, N, O, and P face South in a straight row. K sits third from the right end. L sits second to the left of K. M sits to the immediate right of L. J sits at the extreme right end. O sits exactly between K and J. P is not an immediate neighbor of L. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South (Right end = paper's left). K is at 3. L is second left of K (paper's right) at 5. M is immediate right of L (paper's left) at 4. J is extreme right end at 1. O is between K(3) and J(1) at 2. P is not next to L(5), so P is at 7. N is at 6. Order on paper: J(1), O(2), K(3), M(4), L(5), N(6), P(7). Extreme left end (paper's rightmost) is P.
trick: Navigating 'between' logic with extreme ends solidifies half the board in one step.
tip: Write seat numbers 1 to 7 and fill the knowns directly.

question: U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. U sits second to the right of V. W sits second to the right of U. X sits opposite to U. Y sits to the immediate right of V. Who sits exactly between X and Z?
explanation: V is at 1. U is second right (counter-clockwise) at 5. W is second right of U (counter-clockwise) at 3. X is opposite U(5) at 2. Y is immediate right of V(1) (counter-clockwise) at 6. Z is at 4. Order clockwise: V(1), X(2), W(3), Z(4), U(5), Y(6). Between X(2) and Z(4) is W(3).
trick: Chaining 'second to the right' skips one seat each time, creating a symmetrical star pattern.
tip: Map opposite pairs mentally to verify spacing.

question: F, G, H, I, and J face North. Only two persons sit between F and G. F sits to the left of G. I sits exactly in the middle. H sits to the immediate right of F. Who sits to the immediate left of G?
explanation: With 5 spots, F and G having two people between them means they are at 1 and 4, or 2 and 5. I is in the middle at 3. If F is 2 and G is 5, H (immediate right of F) would be at 3, conflicting with I. Thus, F is at 1 and G is at 4. H is at 2. J is at 5. Order: F(1), H(2), I(3), G(4), J(5). Immediate left of G(4) is I(3).
trick: The middle anchor 'I' prevents the F-G block from taking the 2-5 position.
tip: Test block placements against fixed anchors immediately.

question: A, B, C, D, and E sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits second to the left of D. E sits exactly between A and D. B sits to the immediate right of D. Who sits to the immediate left of C?
explanation: D is at 1. A is second left (clockwise) at 3. E is exactly between A(3) and D(1) at 2. B is immediate right (counter-clockwise) of D(1) at 5. C is at 4. Order clockwise: D(1), E(2), A(3), C(4), B(5). Immediate left of C(4) (clockwise) is B(5).
trick: An 'exactly between' clue effectively completes a sequential trio.
tip: Read the full chain before placing the first person.

question: R, S, T, U, V, and W sit in a row facing South. T sits third from the left end. U sits to the immediate right of T. R sits at the extreme right end. V sits exactly between U and R. S does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits to the immediate left of S?
explanation: South facing. The left end is paper's right side (position 6). T is third from left end at 4. U is immediate right of T (paper's left) at 3. R is extreme right end at 1. V is between U(3) and R(1) at 2. S is not at an end (not 6), so S is at 5. W is at 6. Order on paper: R(1), V(2), U(3), T(4), S(5), W(6). Immediate left of S(5) (paper's right) is W(6).
trick: Identifying 'third from the left end' requires mapping from the correct physical side for South-facing rows.
tip: In South arrangements, right is paper-left, left is paper-right.

question: Ankit, Binny, Charan, Dev, and Esha sit in a row facing North. Dev sits second to the left of Charan. Esha is an immediate neighbor of both Dev and Charan. Ankit sits at the extreme left end. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: Dev is second to the left of Charan. Esha is exactly between them, forming the block Dev-Esha-Charan. Since Ankit is at the extreme left end (position 1), the 3-person block must occupy positions 2, 3, and 4. This places Charan at position 4, leaving Binny to take the extreme right end at position 5.
trick: The phrase 'immediate neighbor of both' perfectly defines the middle person in a rigid 3-seat block.
tip: Identify and group fixed 3-person blocks first before placing them.

question: Maya, Neha, Om, Pari, Qasim, and Ravi sit around a circular table facing the center. Neha sits second to the right of Qasim. Ravi sits opposite to Neha. Om sits to the immediate left of Ravi. Maya is not an immediate neighbor of Qasim. Who sits exactly between Neha and Qasim?
explanation: Place Qasim at 1. Neha is second to the right (counter-clockwise) at 5. Ravi is opposite Neha at 2. Om is immediate left (clockwise) of Ravi at 3. Maya is not adjacent to Qasim(1), so Maya cannot be at 6 and must be at 4. Pari takes the last spot at 6. The person exactly between Neha(5) and Qasim(1) is Pari(6).
trick: Tracing 'opposite' immediately fixes two seats relative to the first placement, simplifying the puzzle rapidly.
tip: Opposite to position 'x' in a 6-person circle is always 'x+3'.

question: L, M, N, O, P, and Q sit in a straight line facing South. N sits third to the right of M. Q sits to the immediate left of N. P sits at the extreme right end. O sits exactly between M and Q. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing (right end is paper's left). P is at 1 (paper's leftmost). N is third to the right of M (towards paper's left). If M is at 5, N is at 2. Q is immediate left of N (paper's right) at 3. O is between M(5) and Q(3) at 4. L is at 6. Order on paper: P(1), N(2), Q(3), O(4), M(5), L(6). Extreme left end (paper's rightmost) is L.
trick: In South-facing setups, 'immediate left' means moving rightwards on the physical paper.
tip: Draw your South-facing line from left to right as 1 to 6.

question: Five friends A, B, C, D, and E sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits second to the left of B. C is an immediate neighbor of B but not of A. D sits to the immediate right of A. Who sits to the immediate left of E?
explanation: B is at 1. A is second left (clockwise) at 3. C is a neighbor of B (2 or 5) but not A(3), so C must be at 5. D is immediate right of A (counter-clockwise) at 4. E is at 2. Order clockwise: B(1), E(2), A(3), D(4), C(5). Immediate left (clockwise) of E(2) is A(3).
trick: A 5-person circle means neighbors of position 1 are at 2 and 5. Position 2 is directly adjacent to 3, restricting placements.
tip: Check negative constraints ('not of A') before assigning a neighbor.

question: S, T, U, V, W, X, and Y face North in a row. S sits fourth to the right of W. V sits exactly in the middle. T sits to the immediate right of S. Y sits at an extreme end. X is an immediate neighbor of V. U is not adjacent to W. Who sits exactly between V and W?
explanation: V is at 4. S is fourth right of W. If W is 1, S is 5. If W is 2, S is 6. T is immediate right of S, so S cannot be 7. If W is 2, S is 6, T is 7, but Y is at an extreme end (must be 1). So Y is 1, W is 2. X is next to V(4) at 3 or 5. U is not next to W(2), so U cannot be 3. U is 5 (meaning X is 3). Order: Y(1), W(2), X(3), V(4), U(5), S(6), T(7). Between V(4) and W(2) is X(3).
trick: The 'fourth to the right' clue plus an extreme end constraint heavily restricts W to a single valid position.
tip: For 7 seats, 'fourth to the right' leaves only two possible anchor setups.

question: G, H, I, J, and K face South in a straight row. I sits exactly in the middle. K sits at the extreme right end. G sits to the immediate left of K. H sits to the immediate left of I. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing means left/right is reversed. K is at the right end (position 1 on paper). G is immediate left of K (paper's right) at 2. I is in the middle at 3. H is immediate left of I (paper's right) at 4. J takes the remaining spot at 5, which is the extreme left end.
trick: Immediate left in a South-facing arrangement translates to moving towards the right side of your page.
tip: Map 'right end' to position 1 on the left edge of your paper.

question: U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. U and V sit opposite each other. W sits to the immediate right of U. X sits to the immediate left of V. Y is not an immediate neighbor of W. Who sits exactly between Z and U?
explanation: U is at 1, V is at 4. W is immediate right of U (counter-clockwise) at 6. X is immediate left of V (clockwise) at 3. The open spots are 2 and 5. Y is not adjacent to W(6), so Y must be at 2. Z is at 5. The person between Z(5) and U(1) is W(6).
trick: Mapping 'immediate right' and 'immediate left' around opposite anchors ensures a quick and balanced fill.
tip: 1 and 4 are opposite. 2 and 5 are opposite. 3 and 6 are opposite.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F face North. E sits at the extreme right end. A sits third to the right of B. D sits to the immediate left of B. C sits to the immediate right of B. F sits exactly between A and C. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: E is at 6. B is an anchor. D is immediate left of B. C is immediate right of B. This forms D-B-C. A is third to the right of B. If B is 2, A is 5. F is exactly between A(5) and C(3), so F is 4. This fits perfectly: D(1), B(2), C(3), F(4), A(5). With E at 6, the order is complete. The extreme left end is D.
trick: The sequence 'D, B, C' and the gap for 'F' precisely lock A into position 5 without needing to test multiple setups.
tip: Build sub-blocks before placing them on the main 1-6 numbered line.

question: P, Q, R, S, and T sit around a circular table facing the center. P sits second to the right of Q. R sits to the immediate right of P. S sits to the immediate left of P. Who sits exactly between Q and S?
explanation: Q is at 1. P is second right (counter-clockwise) at 4. R is immediate right of P (counter-clockwise) at 5. S is immediate left of P (clockwise) at 3. T must be at 2. The person exactly between Q(1) and S(3) is T(2).
trick: Immediate left and right of an anchored person perfectly isolates the remaining seats in a 5-person circle.
tip: Clockwise equals Left, Counter-Clockwise equals Right.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, R, and S sit in a straight line facing South. P sits exactly in the middle. M sits second to the right of P. S sits at the extreme right end. N sits to the immediate left of M. R sits third to the left of N. Q is not an immediate neighbor of P. Who sits exactly between P and R?
explanation: South facing. Right end = paper 1. Left end = paper 7. P is at 4. S is at 1. M is second right of P (paper left) at 2. N is immediate left of M (paper right) at 3. R is third left of N (paper right) at 6 (3+3). Q is not next to P(4), so Q cannot be 5. Q is at 7. O is at 5. Order on paper: S(1), M(2), N(3), P(4), O(5), R(6), Q(7). Between P(4) and R(6) is O(5).
trick: South-facing orientation makes 'second to the right' visually move to the left side of your physical page.
tip: Always convert 'South Right' to 'Paper Left'.

question: V, W, X, Y, and Z face North in a row. Z sits at the extreme left end. Only one person sits between Z and W. Y sits to the immediate right of W. X sits second to the left of Y. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: Z is at 1. One person between Z and W means W is at 3. Y is immediate right of W, so Y is at 4. X is second left of Y, which places X at 2 (the gap between Z and W). V must be at 5. The extreme right end is V.
trick: 'Second to the left of Y' overlaps with the already established empty space between Z and W, filling the gap cleanly.
tip: Read all relative clues before assuming a gap will remain permanently empty.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits opposite to B. C sits second to the left of A. D sits opposite to C. E sits to the immediate right of B. Who sits to the immediate left of D?
explanation: A is at 1, B is opposite at 4. C is second to the left of A (clockwise) at 3. D is opposite C, so D is at 6. E is immediate right of B (counter-clockwise) at 5. F is at 2. Order clockwise: A(1), F(2), C(3), B(4), E(5), D(6). Immediate left of D(6) (clockwise) is A(1).
trick: Two pairs of opposites completely structure the circle, leaving only 2 easily filled spots.
tip: Always draw three intersecting lines to easily visualize a 6-person circle.

question: H, I, J, K, L, and M face South in a row. M sits at the extreme right end. L sits third to the left of M. J sits to the immediate left of L. K sits second to the right of J. I sits to the immediate right of K. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing. M is at 1 (paper's left). L is third left of M (paper's right) at 4. J is immediate left of L (paper's right) at 5. K is second right of J (paper's left) at 3. I is immediate right of K (paper's left) at 2. H must be at 6 (extreme left end). Order on paper: M(1), I(2), K(3), L(4), J(5), H(6).
trick: Alternating left and right movements in a South-facing row can easily cause you to overwrite seats if not tracked numerically.
tip: Map 'South Left' as positive movement and 'South Right' as negative.

question: U, V, W, X, and Y sit around a circular table facing the center. U sits second to the right of X. Y sits exactly between U and X. V sits to the immediate left of X. Who sits to the immediate right of Y?
explanation: X is at 1. U is second right (counter-clockwise) at 4. Y is exactly between U and X. Since it's a 5-person circle, the single gap is at 5. So Y is at 5. V is immediate left of X (clockwise) at 2. W is at 3. Order clockwise: X(1), V(2), W(3), U(4), Y(5). Immediate right of Y(5) (counter-clockwise) is X(1).
trick: In a 5-seat circle, 'exactly between' A and B only fits if they are separated by exactly 1 seat.
tip: 'Second to the right' always leaves exactly one intermediate seat.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V face North in a straight line. R sits third from the right end. P sits second to the left of R. S sits at the extreme left end. T sits exactly between S and P. Q sits to the immediate right of R. V is not an immediate neighbor of Q. Who sits exactly between P and R?
explanation: R is at 5 (third from right). P is second left of R at 3. S is at extreme left at 1. T is between S(1) and P(3) at 2. Q is immediate right of R(5) at 6. V is not next to Q(6), so V is not 7. V must be 4. U is 7. Order: S(1), T(2), P(3), V(4), R(5), Q(6), U(7). Between P(3) and R(5) is V(4).
trick: The phrase 'third from the right end' rigidly sets the anchor at position 5 in a 7-person row.
tip: Number seats 1-7 and place absolute positions first.

question: A, B, C, D, and E sit in a straight line facing North. A sits at the extreme right end. Only two persons sit between A and B. C sits to the immediate left of B. D is not an immediate neighbor of A. Who sits exactly in the middle?
explanation: A is at 5. Two persons between A and B means B is at 2. C is immediate left of B, so C is at 1. D is not next to A(5), so D is not 4. D must be at 3. E takes 4. Order: C(1), B(2), D(3), E(4), A(5). The middle person is D.
trick: The negative constraint 'D is not an immediate neighbor of A' accurately determines the final order of the last two elements.
tip: Extreme ends are the absolute best starting points for 5-person linear setups.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R sit around a circular table facing the center. M sits second to the left of N. P sits opposite to M. Q sits second to the right of P. R is not an immediate neighbor of N. Who sits exactly opposite to N?
explanation: N is at 1. M is second left (clockwise) at 3. P is opposite M at 6. Q is second right (counter-clockwise) of P(6), moving 6 to 5 to 4. So Q is at 4. R is not next to N(1), so R cannot be at 2. R is at 5. O is at 2. Opposite N(1) is Q(4).
trick: Linking relative jumps and opposites seamlessly places every single person without guesswork.
tip: Remember opposite pairs: 1-4, 2-5, 3-6.

question: F, G, H, I, J, and K face South in a straight row. G sits at the extreme left end. I sits third to the right of G. K sits to the immediate left of I. F sits second to the right of K. J is not an immediate neighbor of G. Who sits to the immediate left of F?
explanation: South facing. Left end = paper 6. G is at 6. I is third right of G (paper left) at 3. K is immediate left of I (paper right) at 4. F is second right of K (paper left) at 2. J is not next to G(6), so J cannot be 5. J is at 1. H is at 5. Order on paper: J(1), F(2), I(3), K(4), H(5), G(6). Immediate left of F(2) (paper right) is I(3).
trick: A sequence of relative movements heavily masks the true final positions if not plotted physically.
tip: Immediately map 'South-Left' to 'Paper-Right'.

question: S, T, U, V, and W sit around a circular table facing the center. S sits second to the left of T. V sits exactly between S and T. U sits to the immediate left of S. Who sits to the immediate left of W?
explanation: T is at 1. S is second left (clockwise) at 3. V is between T(1) and S(3), so V is at 2. U is immediate left of S (clockwise), so U is at 4. W is at 5. Order clockwise: T(1), V(2), S(3), U(4), W(5). Immediate left of W(5) (clockwise) is T(1).
trick: In a 5-person circle, an 'exactly between' clue effectively completes a solid block of 3.
tip: Write 1-5 in a circle and trace arrows for L/R before placing.

question: L, M, N, O, P, Q, and R face North in a row. O sits exactly in the middle. M sits second to the right of O. L sits at the extreme left end. N sits exactly between L and Q. Q sits to the immediate left of M. R does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits to the immediate right of R?
explanation: O is at 4. M is second right of O at 6. Q is immediate left of M at 5. L is at 1. N is between L(1) and Q(5). The exact middle of 1 and 5 is 3, so N is at 3. R is not at an extreme end (not 7), so R is at 2. P is at 7. Order: L(1), R(2), N(3), O(4), Q(5), M(6), P(7). Immediate right of R(2) is N(3).
trick: 'Exactly between' two people who are three seats apart perfectly defines the middle seat of that sub-range.
tip: In 7-seat rows, positions 1 and 5 always have position 3 exactly between them.

question: Amit, Bala, Chetan, Dev, and Esha sit in a straight line facing North. Amit sits exactly in the middle of the row. Bala sits to the immediate left of Amit. Chetan sits at the extreme right end. Dev is not an immediate neighbor of Chetan. Who sits to the immediate left of Chetan?
explanation: Amit is exactly in the middle at position 3. Bala is to his immediate left at position 2. Chetan is at the extreme right end at position 5. Dev cannot sit next to Chetan (position 4), so Dev must sit at the extreme left end at position 1. Esha takes the remaining position 4. The person to the immediate left of Chetan (5) is Esha (4).
trick: The negative constraint 'Dev is not an immediate neighbor' perfectly isolates the remaining two seats.
tip: Always place the exact middle and extreme ends first.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, and U sit around a circular table facing the center. P sits exactly opposite to Q. R sits second to the left of P. S sits second to the right of Q. T is not an immediate neighbor of P. Who sits exactly opposite to S?
explanation: Let P be at position 1, so Q is opposite at 4. R is second to the left of P (clockwise) at 3. S is second to the right of Q (counter-clockwise) at 2. T cannot be adjacent to P(1), so T cannot be at 6. Thus, T is at 5. U takes the last spot at 6. The person sitting opposite to S(2) is T(5).
trick: Tracing opposite seats reveals that relative position 2 is always opposite to relative position 5 in a 6-seat circle.
tip: Opposite seats in a 6-person circle always differ by 3.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, R, and S face South in a straight row. M sits exactly in the middle. N sits third to the right of M. O sits to the immediate left of N. P sits second to the left of M. Q sits at the extreme left end. R does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits to the immediate right of S?
explanation: In a South-facing row, Left means moving right on paper, and Right means moving left on paper. M is at 4. N is third to the right of M (paper-left) at 1. O is immediate left of N (paper-right) at 2. P is second to the left of M (paper-right) at 6. Q is at the extreme left end (paper-rightmost) at 7. R is not at an end, so R is at 5. S is at 3. The immediate right of S(3) (paper-left) is O(2).
trick: South-facing right/left rules must be consistently reversed; 'third to the right' means moving towards the physical left edge.
tip: Draw the line 1 to 7 and label 1 as Right End and 7 as Left End.

question: V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. V sits second to the left of W. X sits exactly between V and W. Y sits to the immediate left of V. Who sits to the immediate right of Z?
explanation: Place W at 1. V is second to the left (clockwise) at 3. X is exactly between W(1) and V(3), so X is at 2. Y is to the immediate left of V(3) (clockwise), placing Y at 4. Z takes the remaining spot at 5. The immediate right of Z(5) (counter-clockwise) is Y(4).
trick: 'Second to the left' leaves exactly one gap, perfectly fitting the 'exactly between' condition.
tip: Remember: Clockwise is Left, Counter-Clockwise is Right.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F sit in a row facing North. A sits second from the left end. B sits third to the right of A. C sits to the immediate left of B. D sits at the extreme right end. E does not sit at an extreme end. Who sits exactly between E and B?
explanation: Positions are 1 to 6. A is at 2. B is third to the right of A, so B is at 5. C is to the immediate left of B at 4. D is at the extreme right end at 6. E is not at an extreme end (position 1), so E must be at 3. F is at 1. The order is F, A, E, C, B, D. The person exactly between E(3) and B(5) is C(4).
trick: The negative constraint for E forces it into the middle of the sequence, locking F to the end.
tip: Fill absolute positions first before mapping relative jumps.

question: H, I, J, K, and L sit in a straight line facing South. H sits at the extreme right end. I sits second to the left of H. J sits to the immediate right of I. K sits second to the left of J. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing. The extreme right end is position 1 (on paper). H is at 1. I is second to the left of H (moving right on paper) at 3. J is immediate right of I (moving left on paper) at 2. K is second to the left of J (moving right on paper: 2+2) at 4. L takes position 5. The extreme left end (paper-rightmost) is L.
trick: Alternating left and right movements in a South-facing row can cause you to backtrack over already filled seats if not careful.
tip: Map 'Left' as +1 and 'Right' as -1 on your numbered scratchpad.

question: K, L, M, N, O, and P sit around a circular table facing the center. K sits exactly opposite to N. M sits to the immediate right of N. L sits second to the right of K. O is not an immediate neighbor of L. Who sits exactly opposite to O?
explanation: Place K at 1 and N at 4. M is immediate right of N (counter-clockwise) at 3. L is second to the right of K (counter-clockwise) at 5. O is not a neighbor of L(5), so O cannot be at 6. O must be at 2. P takes position 6. The person exactly opposite O(2) is L(5).
trick: A simple opposite constraint followed by directional logic perfectly aligns the two halves of the circle.
tip: Cross off seat numbers as you fill them to avoid overlaps.

question: T, U, V, W, X, Y, and Z face North in a row. W sits exactly in the middle. X sits third to the right of W. T sits second to the left of W. Y sits to the immediate right of T. Z sits at the extreme left end. U is not an immediate neighbor of W. Who sits exactly between V and X?
explanation: W is at position 4. X is third to the right at 7. T is second to the left at 2. Y is immediate right of T at 3. Z is at the extreme left end at 1. U cannot be next to W(4), so U cannot be at 5. U must be at 6. V takes position 5. The order is Z, T, Y, W, V, U, X. The person exactly between V(5) and X(7) is U(6).
trick: The combination of the middle anchor and extreme ends dictates exactly where the negative constraint (U) resolves.
tip: Use a 7-dash line to visually block out forbidden adjacent seats.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, and U face South in a straight row. P sits third from the right end. Q sits to the immediate left of P. R sits second to the right of P. S sits at the extreme left end. T is not an immediate neighbor of R. Who sits to the immediate right of U?
explanation: South facing. The right end is position 1 (on paper). P is third from the right end at 3. Q is immediate left of P (paper-right) at 4. R is second right of P (paper-left) at 1. The immediate right of U(2) (moving paper-left) is R(1).
trick: Identifying 'third from the right end' requires mapping from the correct physical side for South-facing rows.
tip: Translate all 'South Left/Right' into 'Paper Right/Left' instantly.

question: F, G, H, I, and J sit around a circular table facing the center. F sits second to the left of G. H sits to the immediate left of F. I sits exactly between G and H. Who sits to the immediate left of J?
explanation: Place G at 1. F is second to the left (clockwise) at 3. H is immediate left of F (clockwise) at 4. I sits exactly between G(1) and H(4). In a 5-person circle, the only seat between 1 and 4 is 5. So I is at 5. J takes the remaining seat at 2. The order clockwise is G(1), J(2), F(3), H(4), I(5). The immediate left (clockwise) of J(2) is F(3).
trick: In a 5-person circle, 'between 1 and 4' physically wraps around to seat 5.
tip: Draw the 5 seats symmetrically like a star to see gaps clearly.

question: A, B, C, D, and E face North in a straight line. A sits at the extreme right end. Only two persons sit between A and B. C sits to the immediate right of B. D sits to the immediate left of B. Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
explanation: A is at position 5 (extreme right). Two persons between A and B means B is at position 2. C is immediate right of B, so C is at position 3. D is immediate left of B, so D is at position 1. E takes the remaining position 4. The order is D, B, C, E, A. The person exactly in the middle is C.
trick: A block of three people (D, B, C) can be built independently and then dropped into the remaining slots based on the anchor A.
tip: Lock relative blocks (D-B-C) before assigning them to seat numbers.

question: U, V, W, X, Y, and Z sit around a circular table facing the center. U sits second to the right of V. W sits exactly opposite to V. X sits to the immediate left of U. Y is not an immediate neighbor of W. Who sits exactly opposite to X?
explanation: Place V at 1. U is second to the right (counter-clockwise) at 5. W is opposite V at 4. X is immediate left of U (clockwise) at 6. Y is not next to W(4), so Y cannot be at 3. Y must be at 2. Z takes position 3. The order clockwise is V(1), Y(2), Z(3), W(4), U(5), X(6). The person exactly opposite X(6) is Z(3).
trick: Opposite constraints paired with 'immediate' directional clues rapidly eliminate multiple seat options simultaneously.
tip: Remember opposite pairs: 1-4, 2-5, 3-6.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G face South in a straight row. A sits at the extreme right end. C sits exactly in the middle. B sits exactly between A and the person sitting to the immediate right of C. D sits second to the left of C. E sits to the immediate right of D. F is not an immediate neighbor of A. Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation: South facing (Right end = Paper 1). A is at 1. C is exactly in the middle at 4. The immediate right of C(4) (moving paper-left) is 3. B is exactly between A(1) and position 3, so B is at 2. D is second left of C(4) (paper-right) at 6. E is immediate right of D(6) (paper-left) at 5. F is not next to A(1), so F cannot be 2 (already B). F is at 7 (extreme left end). G takes 3. The extreme left end is F.
trick: A nested positional clue ('between A and the person to the right of C') requires resolving the inner position first.
tip: Resolve complex nested location clues step-by-step from the inside out.

question: M, N, O, P, Q, and R sit in a straight line facing North. M sits third from the left end. N sits second to the right of M. O sits to the immediate left of N. P sits at the extreme left end. Q sits at an extreme end. Who sits to the immediate right of N?
explanation: M is at position 3. N is second to the right of M at 5. O is immediate left of N at 4. P is at the extreme left end at 1. Q is at an extreme end; since P is at 1, Q must be at 6. R takes the remaining position 2. The order is P(1), R(2), M(3), O(4), N(5), Q(6). The immediate right of N(5) is Q(6).
trick: The 'extreme end' clue for Q automatically forces it to the right side since the left is explicitly occupied by P.
tip: Scan all clues for absolute edge placements (Ends) early on.

question: H, I, J, K, and L sit around a circular table facing the center. H sits second to the left of I. J sits to the immediate right of I. K sits exactly between H and J. Who sits to the immediate left of L?
explanation: Place I at 1. H is second to the left (clockwise) at 3. J is immediate right of I (counter-clockwise) at 5. K is exactly between H(3) and J(5), placing K at 4. L takes the remaining position 2. The order clockwise is I(1), L(2), H(3), K(4), J(5). The immediate left (clockwise) of L(2) is H(3).
trick: Defining a person as exactly between two symmetrically placed anchors instantly completes a 3-person cluster.
tip: Plot the anchors first, the middle fills itself naturally.

question: R, S, T, U, and V face South in a straight line. R sits exactly in the middle. S sits to the immediate right of R. T sits at the extreme left end. U sits exactly between R and T. Who sits exactly between V and R?
explanation: South facing. R is in the middle at position 3. S is immediate right of R (paper-left) at 2. T is at the extreme left end (paper-rightmost) at 5. U is exactly between R(3) and T(5), placing U at 4. V takes the remaining position 1. The order on paper is V(1), S(2), R(3), U(4), T(5). The person exactly between V(1) and R(3) is S(2).
trick: The phrasing 'immediate right' in South-facing sequences moves visually to the left on your paper.
tip: Verify exactly which end is 'Left' before placing extreme anchors.

question: A, B, C, D, E, and F sit around a circular table facing the center. A sits exactly opposite to B. C sits second to the right of A. D sits exactly opposite to C. E is not an immediate neighbor of A. Who sits to the immediate left of F?
explanation: Place A at 1, making B opposite at 4. C is second to the right of A (counter-clockwise) at 5. D is opposite C, so D is at 2. E is not a neighbor of A(1), so E cannot be at 6. E must be at 3. F takes position 6. The order clockwise is A(1), D(2), E(3), B(4), C(5), F(6). The immediate left (clockwise) of F(6) is A(1).
trick: Two pairs of opposites (A-B and C-D) structure the circle into rigid thirds, leaving only the negative constraint to resolve.
tip: If A is opposite B, their neighbors are also diametrically opposed.

question: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V sit in a straight line facing North. P sits exactly in the middle. Q sits second to the left of P. R sits second to the right of P. S sits to the immediate left of Q. T sits at the extreme right end. U sits to the immediate left of P. Who sits exactly between P and R?
explanation: P is in the middle at position 4. Q is second to the left of P at 2. R is second to the right of P at 6. S is immediate left of Q at 1. T is at the extreme right end at 7. U is immediate left of P at 3. V takes the remaining position 5. The order is S(1), Q(2), U(3), P(4), V(5), R(6), T(7). The person exactly between P(4) and R(6) is V(5).
trick: Using a central anchor to branch outwards sequentially prevents edge-collision errors in 7-person rows.
tip: Radiate outwards from the middle seat when possible.

question: W, X, Y, Z, A, and B face South in a straight row. W sits second from the right end. X sits third to the left of W. Y sits to the immediate right of X. Z sits at the extreme left end. A sits exactly between W and Y. Who sits at the extreme right end?
explanation: South facing. The right end is position 1 (on paper). W is second from the right end at 2. X is third to the left of W (moving paper-right) at 5. Y is immediate right of X (moving paper-left) at 4. Z is at the extreme left end (paper-rightmost) at 6. A is exactly between W(2) and Y(4), placing A at 3. B takes position 1. The order on paper is B(1), W(2), A(3), Y(4), X(5), Z(6). The extreme right end is B(1).
trick: Resolving 'third to the left' followed by 'immediate right' effectively tracks back one step visually on the paper.
tip: Net movement: 3 Left + 1 Right = 2 Left.

question: M, N, O, P, and Q sit around a circular table facing the center. M sits second to the right of N. O sits to the immediate left of M. P sits exactly between N and O. Who sits to the immediate right of Q?
explanation: Place N at 1. M is second to the right (counter-clockwise) at 4. O is immediate left of M (clockwise) at 3. P is exactly between N(1) and O(3), placing P at 2. Q takes the remaining position 5. The order clockwise is N(1), P(2), O(3), M(4), Q(5). The immediate right (counter-clockwise) of Q(5) is N(1).
trick: In 5-person circles, placing someone 'exactly between' seats 1 and 3 locks them into the only logical intermediate seat.
tip: Always map out the 1-5 loop before declaring an 'exactly between' condition impossible.
